CAP-011.notes: The current UI polls Core; no SSE/live-stream claim. Browser authorization uses HttpOnly device-session cookies and a readable CSRF cookie, never browser storage bearer tokens. QR pairing includes only a non-authorizing challenge identifier; phone sessions remain pending until owner approval and verification-code confirmation. The service worker is network-only and does not cache Core API responses or authorize offline work. Core reports CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, UNKNOWN or DISABLED from its private Office health projection; this does not prove mobile-network reachability. Requests, Decision Inbox, the tabbed Campaign workspace, Runtime, Settings, Access & Devices, Agent Office and the automatic Issues kanban are implemented. Agent Office projects recorded participants only; its Visual Office tab is a deterministic isometric SVG/DOM floor over the same projection, with one avatar per distinct participant_id, role stations, identity-stable slots, keyboard selection and clamped pan/zoom. It adds no simulated activity, and PixiJS remains uninstalled under the recorded renderer decision. Fixture Chromium screenshots exercise the renderer only; real Core/Compose browser acceptance remains NOT_TESTED. The 2026-10-28 studio amendment adds room composition, lighting, furniture and deterministic per-participant avatar appearances, and renders STALE/FINAL/UNKNOWN participants standing rather than at a workstation; Owner visual approval, real Core/Compose browser acceptance and independent acceptance remain NOT_TESTED. Issues has an encrypted GitHub connection, one repository binding per Project, per-page ETag sync with credential-generation fencing and credential-wide backoff, stable issue identity and safe plain-text detail; default-off governed issue intake now has append-only policy revisions, explicit immutable repository/author/label/profile/path/R0/budget acknowledgement, manually selected finite batches, deterministic eligibility, a durable lease/retry queue and reconciliation into ordinary REVIEW_PLAN proposals; execution remains disabled (no Campaign start, provider call or PR write), and a real authorized GitHub read, browser acceptance and issue-to-Campaign execution remain NOT_TESTED. Board ordering, issue writing and comment synchronization remain later work. The Issues view is wired at /issues and component-tested; real browser acceptance remains pending. Unified intake now has a durable Project-scoped request, append-only pre-freeze operator messages, an explicit non-autonomous execution-policy grant, exact profile revision/plan-hash approval, and authoritative Lead withdrawal fencing. Assessment requires an authorized model gateway; no fixture fallback fabricates checks. A real Chromium journey now follows the ordinary intake path through Worker claim, exact candidate, independent verifier, semantic reviewer with model provenance, deterministic Quality Gate, changed files and Core-restart persistence using deterministic fixtures. Exact per-role routing is implemented: the frozen profile Lead route serves intake assessment, the frozen Semantic Reviewer route serves candidate review through candidate → Campaign → start evidence, and the implementer route remains the Campaign authorization route. A Codex App Server connection is executable for implementation but not one-shot assessment/review. Discovered-only model IDs depend on the current Core process discovery cache. Live provider inference, Compose acceptance for the intake path, aggregate cross-role token/cost accounting and independent acceptance remain unimplemented; these are displayed as explicit limits, not inferred state. The legacy Compose stack E2E passes. Factory Office chrome and owned user journeys are available in EN and ES with a persisted locale and 320 px layouts; machine identifiers, statuses, repository content and Core/evidence prose remain untranslated. Docs workspace/editing remains a later slice. Decision Inbox now exposes only Core-backed actions with exact identity guards: approval of a frozen intake plan requires the exact plan hash/profile revision and explicit confirmation; ambiguous model reservations can be released; Lead withdrawal and Campaign cancellation require a reason and confirmation; every mutating action re-reads /office/decisions and aborts when the item revision changed or disappeared. Informational events remain separate and never render action controls. Full-scope Campaign authorization is not posted from the Inbox. Real browser acceptance for the new Inbox actions remains pending. Project onboarding now covers authorized GitHub repository listing and import through the existing encrypted connection, approved-root local import, human Project identity, a Core-backed summary and evidence-based manifest discovery. GitHub App/OAuth installation onboarding is not implemented; fine-grained tokens do not report OAuth scopes, and Office states no installation-wide access. Discovery evidence is advisory and never grants capabilities or check authority. The supported rootless Compose CI also exercises the unified intake lifecycle end to end (request, assessment, exact approval, Worker candidate, verifier/reviewer receipts, Gate ACCEPTED and restart persistence) at implementation `056c502`; it is deterministic-fixture evidence and does not prove live inference, Compose browser acceptance or independent acceptance. The subscription route requires an exact Owner-confirmed, request-scoped subscription admission. Productivity caps are not enforced. A real browser run reached a frozen Lead plan, a governed Campaign and an independent reviewer receipt in this workspace; independent acceptance remains outstanding. The 2026-10-29 visual-polish slice adds semantic shell/content tokens, a deep-navy application rail/top bar, 40/44 px controls and a conversation-first Home with compact Project/profile selectors, one explicit Core-required governed-execution acknowledgement, and lightweight recent-work/decision/status surfaces. Fixture Chromium screenshots at 1440/834/390/320 (EN and ES) verify structure and no horizontal overflow only; they are not acceptance evidence. Product Owner visual acceptance and real Core/Compose browser acceptance remain outstanding, and other Office views keep their existing composition until their own slices. Funding enforcement follow-up (2026-10-29): Core and Worker subscription refusals now provide stable SUBSCRIPTION_FUNDING_BINDING_REQUIRED, SUBSCRIPTION_FUNDING_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED or SUBSCRIPTION_FUNDING_EVIDENCE_INVALID codes with safe error reasons through existing API error surfaces. Worker checks subscription eligibility before historical monetary prerequisites. No subscription dispatch or recovery action is enabled. Dedicated subscription UI, real Core/Compose browser acceptance and pre-Project request admission remain NOT_VERIFIED; a positive monetary envelope cannot substitute for verified subscription funding. Agent Office V3 source candidate a294a43f1c837b721f3b40f4cf217294255742cb adds the continuous studio renderer, stable identity-sorted avatar appearance assignment, a 200-participant regression, and staggered back/front workstation rows with perspective-scaled original vector figures. Chromium fixture captures at 1440, 834 and 390 px are recorded in docs/evidence/agent-office-isometric-v3-2026-10-29/; they do not prove live Core or inspector acceptance. Exact-SHA independent review and Product Owner visual approval remain pending; vector art remains below the approved reference fidelity. The normative shell, Home, Campaign pulse, Agent Office and responsive rules are defined by docs/product/office-ui-standard.md; fixture screenshots are labeled and are not live acceptance. ADR-0034 removes fixed Office model token/time/retry/subscription-cost caps: those values are telemetry, not productivity budgets; authority, egress binding, leases and the Quality Gate remain.

CAP-049.name: Requests and Decision Inbox
CAP-049.job: Start and follow operator requests, including owner-granted R0 autopilot, with human-readable state, see authoritative Core work that needs a decision, and act only through explicit Core operations.
user_actions: start a request, follow its human-readable state and filter the request list by Project or state
inspect decisions, blocked work, unresolved usage and recent events and deep-link each item to its exact Project, Campaign, request, candidate or runtime object
enable one autonomous R0 policy and subscription confirmation, then select that profile and let the Lead assess, freeze and start without per-request approval
approve an exact frozen intake plan only with its plan hash and profile revision, an explicit rationale and confirmation
resolve an AMBIGUOUS or UNKNOWN Core model call with an explicit operator reason
withdraw a frozen Lead request or cancel a Campaign with a reason and proportionate confirmation
open the exact request workspace, Campaign, Project or runtime object without exposing removed pages
cancel an autonomous request or Campaign through the authoritative Core boundary
inspect the bounded, redacted workflow trace for a request: replayed final state, per-step status, ordered event log and structured replay alerts
CAP-049.notes: Requests and decisions are operator-authenticated Core projections; the client does not synthesize state. Removed routes redirect to the closest current workspace, unknown routes return Home, and copied path URLs without a hash redirect for browser navigation. The request list and Decision Inbox filter by Project. A V2 profile whose auto_start policy enables R0 is an autopilot profile: the owner grants the autonomous policy and subscription confirmation once, then Core owns assessment, freeze and start for subsequent requests without per-request UI approval. Manual profiles keep the exact plan approval flow. The Inbox exposes exact-revision intake approval, model-call resolution, Lead withdrawal, Campaign cancellation and navigation; every action revalidates the current decision revision, requires proportionate confirmation and is disabled while Core is unreachable. Full-scope Campaign authorization is not posted from the Inbox. Autonomous Gate repair and provider-session termination remain outside the Inbox. A real Chromium run against Compose exercised the request list, Inbox, filters, deep links and the autonomous R0 path; see docs/evidence/office-autonomy-ux-2026-11-08/manifest.json and docs/evidence/autopilot-r0-2026-11-08/manifest.json. It is implementer evidence, not independent acceptance. No SSE or live-stream claim. WP11 adds an operator-authenticated GET /agentic/requests/{id}/trace read of the latest durable workflow run. It returns a bounded ReplayTrace, per-step rows, a redacted event log ordered by durable sequence, and structured alerts for duplicate sequences, gaps, open steps, terminal/non-terminal state, truncation, malformed rows and replay rejection. Payloads are redacted by Core; free-form step detail is not exposed. The Request workspace renders loading, empty, error/offline, alert, step and long event-log states. Endpoint and component tests pass; real Core/Compose browser acceptance remains NOT_TESTED and this is implementer evidence, not independent acceptance. WP11 review repair: allowlisted payload strings are retained only when they parse as canonical workflow/step/outcome enums, lowercase SHA-256, operational identifiers or numbers/booleans; free-form strings are hashed. Property names outside the canonical payload keys are replaced by a bounded hash label, event IDs must match canonical UUID / workflow-<uuid> / step-<uuid> formats, and the Office refuses invalid payload keys, values or identifier text again. Transition rows with JSON-looking invalid detail or missing/invalid from/to states raise MALFORMED_EVENT, and a rejected replay is shown as unknown rather than in progress. Step rows are bounded to the newest 500 with STEP_TRUNCATED and a visible step-truncation state.

CAP-050.notes: Campaign authorization, Run state, Attempt state and Gate outcome are displayed separately. The Campaign and Request views consume the camelCase V2 `CampaignAuthorizationRecord`: schema version, risk/execution mode, route, authorized paths/tools, `policy.operations`, `policy.progress` and `monetaryEnvelopeId`. Historical V1 caps are optional `legacy` evidence only; missing/empty arrays never crash the Budget & usage tab. The WorkGraph now includes a deterministic dependency layout, keyboard selection and a WorkUnit inspector while preserving the authoritative table. Graph presentation states are explicitly derived from recorded task status and dependencies; malformed data is surfaced, not repaired. Candidate diffs are bounded Core projections from the frozen base to the exact candidate commit/tree: changed-file status, additions/deletions, unified patches, binary/large/non-file omissions, file/patch/byte caps and exact candidate/Gate identity. GitHub pull request reads and actions use the encrypted Core connection; tokens stay server-side. Merge requires explicit confirmation and a fresh PR/check read, never bypasses GitHub branch protection and is never automatic. Real GitHub execution is NOT_TESTED until performed. Participant, tool-event and visual Office projections are provided by Agent Office. The Campaign pulse derives the Lead completion/blocking status from the Gate and Campaign state rather than the raw Lead request state, so an accepted Campaign cannot display a running Lead.

CAP-052.name: Provider and runtime Settings workspace
CAP-052.job: Configure Core-owned provider routes, credentials, models, limits and review policy while distinguishing configuration, connection testing and proven coding inference.
user_actions: select a discovered provider model from a searchable selector while keeping connection details in explicit advanced configuration
save or replace a provider credential without reading it back
revoke a credential after explicit consequence confirmation
set the default route and keep token cost and rate limits in explicit advanced configuration

CAP-052.notes: Credentials are encrypted at rest and never returned to the browser. A saved route is not proof of access. A connection test and model discovery read provider metadata only and are not coding inference. `GET /settings/providers/{provider}/models` returns a typed catalog status (`AVAILABLE`, `ENDPOINT_UNSUPPORTED`, `CREDENTIAL_REJECTED`, `UNREACHABLE`, `INVALID_RESPONSE` or `UNSUPPORTED`) with source, catalog URL and observation time, a bounded model list, no proxy and no redirects. `opencode-go` reads its sibling `/inference/go/v1/models` catalog without sending the inference credential; a missing catalog is not a credential finding, and a 401/403 is only a signal for that catalog endpoint. Codex App Server discovery is `UNSUPPORTED` by design. Discovery and the last-known snapshot are an in-memory Core cache and are not persisted. ChatGPT OAuth remains visibly blocked or not applicable. Provider revisions do not rewrite frozen Campaign bindings. Ordinary provider configuration uses a searchable model selector; base URL, manual model IDs, token/cost/rate limits and connection details are explicit advanced controls. Home and Execution Profiles no longer require turn, attempt, session, token, cost or deadline controls; Core V2 technical operation limits remain enforceable.

CAP-054.notes: Session cookie material is HttpOnly. CSRF uses the dedicated readable SameSite cookie. Pairing challenge IDs do not grant authority and are stripped from browser history before phone requests. The phone receives a separate hashed poll capability, and Core creates a session only after the authenticated owner submits the matching code. CAP-064.name: Bounded repair orchestration

The repair is a new request, not an in-place mutation of the rejected Campaign.

CAP-060.notes: The Planner and Spec Manager are bounded Lead-route model calls with distinct purpose and typed schemas. Core validates the graph and compiles the frozen identities deterministically. Planning is lane-routed and every lane requires a plan review; Core auto-approves only within the frozen policy and otherwise requires an authenticated owner decision. Planning artifacts are exact revisions bound to a SHA-256. Reviewer findings are durable dispositions and an OPEN finding blocks the Gate even when the reviewer receipt passed. A frozen specification is immutable; authoring creates a new revision. Browser acceptance for the new plan-review and finding surfaces remains NOT_TESTED.
